newsitem.title: INDONESIA: JAKARTA STOCKS END 3.13 PCT DOWN ON RATES, MARGIN.
newsitem.headline: JAKARTA STOCKS END 3.13 PCT DOWN ON RATES, MARGIN.

text.p: Indonesia's Finance Minister Mari'e Muhammad paid a surprise visit to the stock exchange on Thursday to bolster confidence as the market index suffered one of its sharpest one day falls.
Brokers and analysts said the market was hit by accumulated concern over higher interest rates, new margin finance regulations and payments due on large rights issues.
The composite index ended down 21.92 points, or 3.13 percent, at 677.94 points after touching a low of 673.72. Decliners led advancers by 165 to 12 with 21 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 506 billion rupiah.
"It certainly is one of the market's biggest one-day falls. The plunge reminds us of the sharp fall last year after the July 27 riots," one broker with a foreign brokerage firm said.
The Jakarta composite index fell 20.06 points to close at 540.74 points on Monday, July 29, after touching a low for the day of 527.77 following the worst riots the capital in more than two decades.

Bank Indonesia's recent policy of increasing short-term rates of central bank certificates (SBIs) and staying out of the short-term securities market (SBPUs) was aimed at reducing speculative attacks on the rupiah, analysts said.
